operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-101. Executive agencies shall emphasize procurement set-asides in labor surplus areas in order to strengthen our Nation's economy.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-101

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-102. Labor surplus area procurements shall be consistent with this Order and, to the extent funds are available, the priorities of Section 15 of the Small Business Act, as amended by Public Law 9589 (15 U.S.C. 644).

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-102

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-201. The Administrator shall coordinate with and advise State and local officials with regard to Federal efforts to encourage procurements in labor surplus areas with the aim of fostering economic development in labor surplus areas.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-201

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-202. The Administrator shall establish specific labor surplus area procurement targets for Executive agencies in consultation with the heads of those agencies.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-202

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-203. In cooperation with the heads of Executive agencies, the Administrator shall encourage the use of set-asides or other appropriate methods for meeting procurement targets in labor surplus areas.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-203

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-204. The Administrator shall report every six months to the President on the progress of the agencies in achieving the procurement targets.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-204

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-301. The Secretary of Labor shall classify and designate labor markets which are labor surplus areas. The Secretary shall provide labor market data to the heads of agencies and State and local officials in order to promote the development of business opportunities in labor surplus areas.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-301

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-302. The heads of Executive agencies shall cooperate with the Administrator in carrying out his responsibilities for labor surplus area programs and shall provide the information necessary for setting procurement targets and recording achievement. They shall keep the Administrator informed of plans and programs which affect labor surplus procurements, with particular attention to opportunities for minority firms.

original_source.page_or_item: American Presidency Project web page (transcription; not an official edition); APP node 248490; common-crawl capture 2025-09-08T07:35:56Z; Sec. 1-302

operative_clauses.original_operative_text: 1-303. In accord with Section 6 of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act (41 U.S.C. 405), the Administrator for Federal Procurement Policy shall be responsible for the overall direction and oversight of the policies affecting procurement programs for labor surplus areas.
